claude_only.name: Which authoritative master system issues the identifier for this configuration, and what is that identifier?
What governed namespace or reverse-DNS name distinguishes this configuration from a same-named configuration published by someone else?
Is this a system instruction, a parameterised prompt template, an agent definition, a tool-grant set, or a composite of these?
Which display titles, slugs or aliases resolve to this configuration, and which of them are guaranteed stable?
What algorithm-qualified digest identifies the exact content of this configuration revision?
Which canonical serialisation was digested so the same logical configuration yields the same digest in any store?
Which regions are excluded from the digest because they resolve only at run time?
Which version scheme governs this configuration and what change classes force a major increment?
Which consumers pin this configuration by exact revision rather than by a version range?
Which protocol or interface revisions does this configuration declare itself compatible with?
May a released version be edited in place, and if not, how are corrections issued?
Who must approve promotion to production and on what evidence?
When was this revision authored, approved, released and withdrawn, each recorded as a separate instant?
What notice period applies before this configuration is withdrawn from service?
Which discrete instruction blocks make up this configuration and what role does each carry?
Which block is delivered to the model as the system or developer instruction before any user input?
Which named arguments does this template accept and which of them are required?
What rendering or substitution step turns the template plus arguments into the final message sequence?
What happens when a required argument is missing or fails schema validation?
Which parent or base configurations does this revision import, extend or override?
When more than one configuration applies to the same working scope, which one wins?
Which fragments are shared with other configurations and therefore change together?
Which locale, tenant or channel variants exist and how is one selected at run time?
At which authority level does each instruction block sit relative to platform, developer and user instructions?
Which instructions may an end user override and which are non-negotiable for this deployment?
How is a conflict between two instructions of equal authority resolved?
Which inbound content channels are declared untrusted and stripped of instruction authority?
What structural markers separate retrieved or tool-returned content from configuration instructions?
What evidence shows this revision was tested against direct and indirect prompt injection?
What does the runtime do when injected instructions are detected mid-run?
Which model and provider is this configuration pinned to, if any?
If no exact model is pinned, which capability priorities and hints drive selection?
What must be re-validated when the underlying model changes beneath a pinned configuration?
Which decoding parameters are set and what value does each take?
Which of these parameters may the runtime silently ignore, clamp or reject?
What output format does this configuration require and is it enforced by a schema?
Which schema dialect governs the declared output structure?
Which named tools may this configuration call and from which server does each come?
Which input and output schemas were bound to each granted tool at release time?
How are collisions between identically named tools from different servers disambiguated?
Which tools are explicitly denied even when the runtime offers them?
Which granted tools are annotated read-only, destructive, idempotent or open-world?
On what basis is the server supplying those annotations treated as trusted?
Which tool calls require explicit human confirmation before execution?
What invocation or rate limits apply per tool under this configuration?
Which resources, roots or knowledge collections may be read into context?
What context-inclusion mode applies and may the runtime narrow it for privacy reasons?
Which persistent memory stores may this configuration write to and with what scope?
Which servers does this configuration bind to, at what endpoint and over which transport?
Which authorization scopes are requested and which declared capability justifies each one?
How are credentials referenced without being embedded in instruction text?
What happens when a bound server changes its tool list after this revision was released?
Which behaviours does this configuration require, forbid or make conditional?
Which of those constraints are enforced outside the model rather than by instruction text alone?
What refusal or safe-completion behaviour is specified for out-of-scope requests?
Does any instruction block contain a secret, credential or connection string?
What is the declared impact if the full instruction text is disclosed to an end user?
Which independent output inspection verifies compliance instead of relying on the prompt?
Which actions require a human in the loop able to deny them?
What must be shown to the reviewer before an approval decision is taken?
Which role is competent and empowered to intervene, and how is that competence assured?
How is an override, edit or denial recorded?
What is the maximum number of autonomous steps or tool-loop iterations permitted?
What token, cost and wall-clock budget bounds a single run under this configuration?
What terminates a run that exceeds its budget and what state is left behind?
Which evaluation suites were run against this exact revision digest?
What acceptance thresholds had to be met before release was permitted?
Which model build and runtime version were used during evaluation?
How long does this evaluation evidence remain valid before it must be repeated?
What adversarial or red-team testing was performed against this configuration?
Which attack classes were explicitly out of scope for that testing?
Which findings remain open at release and who accepted the residual risk?
Which agents authored or revised this configuration and on whose behalf did they act?
Which activity generated this revision and from which prior entity was it derived?
Was any part of this configuration machine-generated, and by which system?
When did the authoring activity start and end, as distinct from when the record was ingested?
Which signed attestation binds a builder identity to this revision digest?
Which external parameters and resolved dependencies produced the released artifact?
Which models, datasets, tools and third-party prompt components does this configuration depend on?
How does a consumer verify the attestation before loading the configuration?
In which environments and tenants is this revision currently active?
What rollout strategy governs exposure and what share of traffic sees this revision?
From when until when was this revision effective in each environment?
Which prior revision is the designated rollback target?
What mechanism disables this configuration immediately without a redeploy?
Which telemetry attribute carries the exact configuration revision used by a run?
Are instruction texts recorded in telemetry, and under what opt-in and redaction rules?
How long are run records kept so a run can still be traced back to its configuration?
Which entry in the organisational AI system inventory records this configuration?
Which duties are separated so that the author is not the sole approver?
Does the system driven by this configuration fall into a regulated risk class in any applicable jurisdiction?
Which technical-documentation elements must record the key design choices captured here?
Which jurisdictions and effective dates apply to those duties?
What confidentiality class applies to the instruction text of this configuration?
Which principals may read, propose, approve or publish revisions of it?
Which fields must be redacted before the configuration is shared with a deployer or auditor?
What is logged whenever the configuration is read or exported?
How long must superseded revisions be retained to support audit and reproducibility?
What deletes a revision and what tombstone survives deletion?
Which legal hold or regulatory minimum overrides the normal retention period?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier names this configuration in the registry or agent platform of record?
What content digest of the canonical instruction, tool, parameter, and guardrail payload must a run pin so replay does not depend on a mutable latest pointer?
What non-date version label or stored-prompt version is published, and is it distinct from the master identifier?
When was this configuration version created or published as an event, and when was it observed or ingested if those instants differ?
Is this payload an instruction stack, a user-selectable prompt template, a skill package, a tool catalog binding, a stored-prompt reference, or a composite agent configuration?
What intended purpose, user population, and prohibited uses bound this configuration?
Is the prompt fixed by the deployer, editable by operators, or dynamically generated per request, and who may edit it?
Which fields may appear on a public discovery card versus remaining in the operational instruction body?
Which authority layers does this configuration actually supply, and which layers are inherited from the model provider?
What explicit override policy applies when developer, user, skill, and retrieved-content instructions conflict?
Which root-level refusals or legal-compliance rules cannot be overridden by this configuration?
Are there locale- or age-specific provider-system rules that change applicable instructions without a developer edit?
What review, red-team, or dual-control evidence authorized activation or rollback of this version?
Under what incident conditions is the configuration frozen, and who may lift the freeze or force a rollback?
Which instruction messages exist by role and purpose, and what is the verbatim or referenced body of each?
What role, capabilities, limitations, tone, and tool-use instructions are declared for the scenario?
If instructions are computed at request time, what function, inputs, and non-model local context are allowed to shape them?
What token or character budget is allocated to static instructions so they do not starve task context?
What named arguments or variables may be substituted, which are required, and what types and examples apply?
Does this configuration reference a vendor-stored prompt object, and which version must be sent on every turn rather than assumed from conversation state?
From where may variable values be supplied, and which sources are untrusted for substitution into instructions?
How are missing, extra, or injection-bearing argument values rejected before messages are materialized?
What skill name, description, license, compatibility, and directory identity uniquely identify each bound skill version?
Under what conditions is a skill activated, and which instruction body, scripts, and references may then load?
Does the skill declare experimental allowed-tools, and how is that reconciled with the host configuration allowlist?
Was the skill validated against naming and frontmatter rules, and what validator and result apply?
In what order are provider, deployer, stored-prompt, skill, example, and variable layers concatenated or overridden to produce the effective stack?
What digest identifies the fully materialized instruction stack after substitution, distinct from the unevaluated template digest?
If the composed stack exceeds the context budget, what is dropped first and is that drop recorded?
Which few-shot or skill examples are part of configuration versus live conversation history?
Which tools are bound, with names, titles, descriptions, and input and output schemas?
From which servers, libraries, or inline functions does each tool originate, and which catalog version is pinned?
If a backing server can emit listChanged, does this configuration freeze the catalog or accept live additions?
Are arguments and structured results validated against the declared schemas before and after invocation?
What allowlist, denylist, and tool-choice setting constrain which tools the model may request?
Are tool annotations treated as untrusted hints, and what independent risk class is assigned to each tool?
Which tool classes require human confirmation, and what timeout, rate limit, and audit apply?
Which bound tools may mutate state, exfiltrate data, or reach an open world, regardless of author hints?
Which model identifier is requested, and may a runner override it without creating a new configuration version?
What temperature, top_p, top_k, max tokens, penalties, stop sequences, seed, stream flag, and reasoning level apply?
Who set each generation parameter and whether it came from a stored prompt, agent defaults, or a runner override?
Is reproducible sampling required, and if so how is seed combined with the configuration digest without treating seed as an identifier?
What structured-output schema or MIME types must responses satisfy, and what happens on violation?
Which default input and output modalities are enabled, and which are overridden per skill?
Which other configurations or agents may be handed off to, with what descriptions and constraints?
Which skills are advertised on a discovery card versus only available inside this operational configuration?
What query and output classes must this configuration refuse, and where is that encoded besides natural-language instructions?
Which input and output guardrails, content filters, and thresholds are bound to this version?
Do guardrail failures fail closed, fail open, or escalate to a human, and is that logged?
What red-team or evaluation evidence last showed these refusals still hold after the instruction or tool-list change?
What technical controls separate untrusted user or retrieved content from higher-authority instructions?
Has the instruction body been scanned to exclude credentials, connection strings, and security-by-obscurity rules?
Who may read the operational instruction body versus the public skill or Agent Card description?
Who may edit system instructions, guardrails, or tool lists, and is that action audited?
What identifiers must an agent run record to pin this exact configuration, including digest and not only a latest alias?
May instruction text and tool definitions be copied into telemetry, and under what privacy policy?
How long are inactive configuration versions retained for replay, and what legal or audit hold extends that?
What happens to already-pinned runs if this version is deleted, tombstoned, or redacted?
Which external schemas is this configuration mapped to, and with what field-level mapping evidence?
Is any conformance to MCP, A2A, Agent Skills, or OTel actually claimed, and what test evidence supports it?
Which recorded conflicts (prompt control, system-layer meaning, version-as-date, hosted versus repo prompts) affect this instance?
Which storage or interface projection carries this instance, without treating that projection as the semantic model?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
